title: Procrastinating einselection in non-Markovian quantum dynamics
authors: Michael J. Moody, Tara Kalsi, Agung Budiyono, Sebastian Deffner
abstract: Among the processes governed by open-system and dissipative quantum dynamics, environment-induced superselection, or einselection, is particularly foundational, since it describes the formation of a preferred set of pointer states through environmental monitoring and ultimately the emergence of classicality. Especially in the context of Quantum Darwinism, einselection can be studied in terms of the motion of an observable towards its pointer value. To this end, we derive a quantum speed limit for observables for finite-dimensional systems governed by differentiable time-local open dynamics. We identify two mechanisms through which non-Markovianity can enhance observable speed: direct dissipative motion supported by population retention or revival, and indirect enhancement through restoration of the asymmetry available for coherent motion. For permanent einselection, this delays the emergence of the pointer basis due to accumulated negativity.
summary: This theoretical paper derives a quantum speed limit for observables undergoing non-Markovian open quantum dynamics. It analyzes how environmental dissipation affects the process of einselection, showing that non-Markovian effects can enhance or delay the approach to classicality. The findings establish a quantitative link between the accumulated negativity of the decoherence rate and the time delay in pointer state formation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the rate at which a quantum system approaches classicality (einselection) within the framework of non-Markovian open quantum dynamics.
main_result: Non-Markovianity can both accelerate and delay the einselection process, with the delay being bounded by the accumulated negativity of the canonical decoherence rate.
method: The authors derive and analyze a quantum speed limit for observables by decomposing the time evolution into coherent and dissipative current contributions.
model_or_system: The analysis concerns finite-dimensional quantum systems governed by open-system dynamics described by time-local master equations, incorporating both Hamiltonian evolution and environmental dissipation.

important_parameters: Non-Markovianity (signaled by $\gamma_\mu(t) < 0$), accumulated negativity ($F(0,t)$), and the time-local generator $L_t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to differentiable time-local open dynamics, and the speed limit derivation relies on specific mathematical inequalities.

paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the observable speed limit in open systems, then analyzing the decomposition of the evolution into coherent and dissipative currents, and finally comparing the speed enhancement in non-Markovian (CP-indivisible) dynamics against Markovian references.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental connection between environmental coupling, the emergence of classicality (einselection), and the fundamental constraints on quantum evolution (QSLs) in non-Markovian regimes, which is central to modern open quantum systems theory.
